speaker_title: Address by Ms. Simonetta Sommaruga, President of the Swiss Confederation

paragraphs.text: Mr President of the General Assembly,
paragraphs.raw_text: Mr President of the General Assembly,

paragraphs.text: Mr Secretary-General,
paragraphs.raw_text: Mr Secretary-General,

paragraphs.text: Distinguished Heads of State and government,
paragraphs.raw_text: Distinguished Heads of State and government,

paragraphs.text: Excellencies,
paragraphs.raw_text: Excellencies,

paragraphs.text: Ladies and gentlemen,
paragraphs.raw_text: Ladies and gentlemen,

paragraphs.text: There are moments that leave their mark for generations. The founding of the United Nations seventy-five years ago was one such moment. For this, we can be grateful to our parents.
paragraphs.raw_text:
There are moments that leave their mark for generations. The founding of the 
United Nations seventy-five years ago was one such moment. For this, we can be 
grateful to our parents.

paragraphs.text: Are we nevertheless permitted to take a critical look at the UN today? — Yes, we are... We even have to.
paragraphs.raw_text:
Are we nevertheless permitted to take a critical look at the UN today? — Yes, 
we are... We even have to.

paragraphs.text: In fact, seventy-five years on and there are still wars, there are more refugees and displaced people than ever before, there is a climate crisis currently without a solution, millions are going hungry and we haven’t achieved gender equality.
paragraphs.raw_text:
In fact, seventy-five years on and there are still wars, there are more refugees 
and displaced people than ever before, there is a climate crisis currently without a 
solution, millions are going hungry and we haven’t achieved gender equality.

paragraphs.text: We could criticise the UN for this — but who are we really talking about, when we blame “the UN”? We are in fact talking about ourselves, because the UN is its Member States. And it is often Member States that stand in the way of the UN’s work. They block decisions or refuse to implement them, undermine resolutions or flout their principles.
paragraphs.raw_text:
We could criticise the UN for this  — but who are we really talking about, 
when we blame “the UN”? We are in fact talking about ourselves, because the UN is 
its Member States. And it is often Member States that stand in the way of the UN’s 
work. They block decisions or refuse to implement them, undermine resolutions or 
flout their principles.

paragraphs.text: This weakens the UN. And it weakens all of us, too. If we want a strong UN, then we — Member States — must strongly support the organisation and work together to pursue its objectives. Because the goals of the UN are our goals.
paragraphs.raw_text:
This weakens the UN. And it weakens all of us, too. If we want a strong UN, 
then we  — Member States  — must strongly support the organisation and work 
together to pursue its objectives. Because the goals of the UN are our goals.

paragraphs.text: Ladies and gentlemen,
paragraphs.raw_text: Ladies and gentlemen,

paragraphs.text: We live in an era marked by geopolitical tensions. Many States are also increasingly polarised in their internal affairs.
paragraphs.raw_text:
We live in an era marked by geopolitical tensions. Many States are also 
increasingly polarised in their internal affairs.

paragraphs.text: More than ever, the UN is indispensable for the promotion of peace and security in the world. It embodies the causes of human rights, sustainable development and a world governed by the rule of law. We would do well to work together to achieve the goals of the UN because they benefit all of us and they make us stronger.
paragraphs.raw_text:
More than ever, the UN is indispensable for the promotion of peace and security 
in the world. It embodies the causes of human rights, sustainable development and a 
world governed by the rule of law. We would do well to work together to achieve the 
goals of the UN because they benefit all of us and they make us stronger.

paragraphs.text: My country is proud to contribute to the achievement of the UN’s goals, even if it is not always easy. It is difficult to translate the goals we have set ourselves – on climate or gender equality for example – into national policy. But that is why all of us politicians are elected: to offer our respective populations and humanity as a whole a decent life in freedom and security.
paragraphs.raw_text:
My country is proud to contribute to the achievement of the UN’s goals, even 
if it is not always easy. It is difficult to translate the goals we have set ourselves – on 
climate or gender equality for example – into national policy. But that is why all of us 
politicians are elected: to offer our respective populations and humanity as a whole a 
decent life in freedom and security.

paragraphs.text: My country also advocates for an international order regulated by the rule of law. We are committed to international humanitarian law and to the prevention of conflicts, and we provide good offices wherever they are desired. My country is prepared to take on more responsibilities, which is why for the first time, Switzerland
paragraphs.raw_text:
My country also advocates for an international order regulated by the rule 
of law. We are committed to international humanitarian law and to the prevention 
of conflicts, and we provide good offices wherever they are desired. My country is 
prepared to take on more responsibilities, which is why for the first time, Switzerland

paragraphs.text: is a candidate for a non-permanent seat on the Security Council for the period 2023–2024.
paragraphs.raw_text:
is a candidate for a non-permanent seat on the Security Council for the period 
2023–2024.

paragraphs.text: Switzerland of course wholeheartedly supports the Secretary General’s appeal for a global ceasefire. But beyond such an appeal, is there anything else we can do?
paragraphs.raw_text:
Switzerland of course wholeheartedly supports the Secretary General’s appeal 
for a global ceasefire. But beyond such an appeal, is there anything else we can do?

paragraphs.text: We must put even more effort into preventing conflicts. Here too, human rights must remain at the centre of our action. “International Geneva” also contributes to conflict prevention, for example by hosting the Human Rights Council and the Arms Trade Treaty Secretariat.
paragraphs.raw_text:
We must put even more effort into preventing conflicts. Here too, human rights 
must remain at the centre of our action. “International Geneva” also contributes to 
conflict prevention, for example by hosting the Human Rights Council and the Arms 
Trade Treaty Secretariat.

paragraphs.text: By prosecuting the worst crimes, the International Criminal Court is contributing to uphold international humanitarian law. We reaffirm here our support for the International Criminal Court as an integral part of a rules-based international order. To facilitate debate on the best ways to adhere to these humanitarian norms, Switzerland was one of the first countries to publish a voluntary report on its national implementation. My country would welcome it if other countries followed.
paragraphs.raw_text:
By prosecuting the worst crimes, the International Criminal Court is 
contributing to uphold international humanitarian law. We reaffirm here our support 
for the International Criminal Court as an integral part of a rules-based international 
order. To facilitate debate on the best ways to adhere to these humanitarian norms, 
Switzerland was one of the first countries to publish a voluntary report on its national 
implementation. My country would welcome it if other countries followed.

paragraphs.text: While it is right to try to prevent conflicts and to seek to mitigate their worst humanitarian consequences, it is also crucial to find lasting solutions to the conflicts that are ongoing. As the capital of peace, “International Geneva” contributes to this by providing a space for dialogue between the parties to a conflict.
paragraphs.raw_text:
While it is right to try to prevent conflicts and to seek to mitigate their worst 
humanitarian consequences, it is also crucial to find lasting solutions to the conflicts 
that are ongoing. As the capital of peace, “International Geneva” contributes to this 
by providing a space for dialogue between the parties to a conflict.

paragraphs.text: Switzerland’s peace policy draws on essential characteristics of my country’s political culture, such as power-sharing, openness to dialogue, tolerance and consideration of everyone’s interests. In the future, Switzerland intends to further step up its capacities and expertise in mediation and facilitation in order to support those who wish to end conflicts through dialogue.
paragraphs.raw_text:
Switzerland’s peace policy draws on essential characteristics of my country’s 
political culture, such as power-sharing, openness to dialogue, tolerance and 
consideration of everyone’s interests. In the future, Switzerland intends to further 
step up its capacities and expertise in mediation and facilitation in order to support 
those who wish to end conflicts through dialogue.

paragraphs.text: Ladies and gentlemen,
paragraphs.raw_text: Ladies and gentlemen,

paragraphs.text: While “International Geneva” contributes to peace and security in the world, it is also the seat of the World Health Organization, which has played such a crucial role since the onset of the COVID-19 pandemic.
paragraphs.raw_text:
While “International Geneva” contributes to peace and security in the world, 
it is also the seat of the World Health Organization, which has played such a crucial 
role since the onset of the COVID-19 pandemic.

paragraphs.text: The current health crisis has caused untold suffering in the world. The most vulnerable have been hit hardest: the child in the overcrowded displacement camp; the single mother who has lost her job; the young adult whose job prospects have been destroyed; or elderly people and the sick, who are particularly at risk.
paragraphs.raw_text:
The current health crisis has caused untold suffering in the world. The most 
vulnerable have been hit hardest: the child in the overcrowded displacement camp; 
the single mother who has lost her job; the young adult whose job prospects have been 
destroyed; or elderly people and the sick, who are particularly at risk.

paragraphs.text: My country is coping with this pandemic as best it can.
paragraphs.raw_text: My country is coping with this pandemic as best it can.

paragraphs.text: The World Health Organization plays a central part in fighting the pandemic. As host state of the WHO and other international health organisations, Switzerland is committed to ensuring that they can take effective action. For this to happen, the WHO must have sufficient resources and the support of all of us to carry out its reforms. Is it fair to demand so much from this organisation when 80% of its funding comes from voluntary contributions?
paragraphs.raw_text:
The World Health Organization plays a central part in fighting the pandemic. 
As host state of the WHO and other international health organisations, Switzerland 
is committed to ensuring that they can take effective action. For this to happen, the 
WHO must have sufficient resources and the support of all of us to carry out its 
reforms. Is it fair to demand so much from this organisation when 80% of its funding 
comes from voluntary contributions?

paragraphs.text: Beyond the necessary fight against the current pandemic, we must think now about the world that will emerge from this crisis and that cannot entirely be yesterday’s. If every crisis is a suffering, it is also a moment of change that allows us to reinvent ourselves.
paragraphs.raw_text:
Beyond the necessary fight against the current pandemic, we must think 
now about the world that will emerge from this crisis and that cannot entirely be 
yesterday’s. If every crisis is a suffering, it is also a moment of change that allows us 
to reinvent ourselves.

paragraphs.text: So let’s reinvent ourselves, keeping in mind the goals we set for ourselves when the UN was created seventy-five years ago.
paragraphs.raw_text:
So let’s reinvent ourselves, keeping in mind the goals we set for ourselves 
when the UN was created seventy-five years ago.

paragraphs.text: Ladies and gentlemen,
paragraphs.raw_text: Ladies and gentlemen,

paragraphs.text: There are moments that leave their mark for generations. Such moments require decisive and courageous action. This is true today. From my country’s perspective, the most urgent tasks are to implement the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development and the Paris Agreement, and to step up our efforts for peace.
paragraphs.raw_text:
There are moments that leave their mark for generations. Such moments require 
decisive and courageous action. This is true today. From my country’s perspective, 
the most urgent tasks are to implement the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development 
and the Paris Agreement, and to step up our efforts for peace.

paragraphs.text: It is up to us — the political representatives of our countries — to take the right decisions for the good of our fellow human beings and our planet. Let us assume this responsibility.
paragraphs.raw_text:
It is up to us — the political representatives of our countries — to take the 
right decisions for the good of our fellow human beings and our planet. Let us assume 
this responsibility.

paragraphs.text: Let us strengthen the UN’s capacity to act, and ensure that the decisions we make today will be a source of pride for generations of tomorrow.
paragraphs.raw_text:
Let us strengthen the UN’s capacity to act, and ensure that the decisions we 
make today will be a source of pride for generations of tomorrow.
